name: Dead-Letter + Retry System - Failure Capture, Backoff & Escalation

parameters.content:
## Dead-Letter + Retry System - Failure Capture, Backoff & Escalation

### How it works

This workflow receives failed job/message payloads (from another workflow's error path, a webhook, or a manual test run), records every failure in a dead-letter store, and retries each one with exponential backoff up to a configured attempt limit. Retries that succeed are marked resolved and logged. Retries that keep failing are moved to a permanent dead-letter queue, escalated to Slack/on-call, and excluded from further automatic retries so they don't loop forever.

### Setup steps

- Point the 'Receive Failed Job' webhook (or the upstream workflow's Error Workflow setting) at this workflow so failures land here automatically.
- Connect your dead-letter store credentials (Google Sheets/Postgres/etc.) for 'Log to Dead-Letter Store' and related record updates.
- Connect the downstream service credentials the retry actually calls in 'Retry Original Operation' - this should call the same endpoint/action that originally failed.
- Connect Slack credentials for retry-exhausted escalation and the resolution/activity feed.
- Configure the Set Configuration Parameters node: max retry attempts, backoff base/multiplier, retry-eligible error codes, and the on-call Slack channel.
- Configure 'Sweep Pending Retries' schedule interval to match how quickly you want failed jobs retried.

### Reliability notes

- Every failure is written to the dead-letter store BEFORE any retry is attempted, so nothing is lost even if the retry itself crashes the workflow.
- Backoff delay is computed deterministically (base * multiplier^attempt, capped) so retries space themselves out instead of hammering a struggling downstream service.
- Jobs that exceed max attempts are marked 'exhausted' and never picked up by the sweep again, preventing infinite retry loops.
- Consider attaching an n8n Error Workflow to this workflow itself so a failure inside the retry system is never silently swallowed.

### Customization

Adjust maxRetryAttempts, backoff timing, which error types are considered retryable vs. immediately fatal, the dead-letter schema, and the escalation channel/routing to match your incident process.

## Receive failed job

Entry point that accepts a failed job payload from an upstream workflow's error path, a webhook, or a manual test run, then normalizes shared configuration and failure metadata.

## Capture to dead-letter store

Writes every incoming failure to the dead-letter store first, before any retry is attempted, so a failing retry can never cause the original failure to be lost.

## Classify and gate retry eligibility

Decides whether this failure type is retryable at all and whether the job still has attempts remaining, branching accordingly before any backoff or retry work happens.

## Exhaust and escalate

Marks the job permanently exhausted in the dead-letter store when it is not retryable or has used up all attempts, then escalates to Slack/on-call so a human can intervene.

## Backoff and retry

Computes an exponential backoff delay based on the attempt count, waits, then re-attempts the original operation against the downstream service.

## Evaluate retry outcome

Inspects the retry attempt's result and branches on whether the operation ultimately succeeded or failed again.

## Confirm resolution

Marks the dead-letter record resolved and notifies Slack when a retried job finally succeeds.

## Requeue for another attempt

Increments the attempt count on the dead-letter record and sends the job back into the retry-eligibility check to try again, subject to the max attempts limit.

## Periodic sweep

On a schedule, pulls any dead-letter records still pending retry (e.g. left mid-backoff after a restart) and feeds them back into the same eligibility check so nothing is stranded.
